Definition
[Pseudo-Riemannian metric and index]

Source: petersen:page-0024, petersen:page-0025 ↗ def:pet-ch1-riemannian-manifold

A semi-Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian metric is a smooth symmetric bilinear form $g$ on the tangent spaces such that for each nonzero $v$ some $w$ satisfies $g(v,w)\ne 0$. Each $T_pM$ admits a splitting $P\oplus N$ on which $g$ is respectively positive and negative definite. Although $P,N$ are not canonical, their dimensions are locally constant; on connected $M$, the index is the common value $\dim N$.
